evidence: No tool call; agent said 'I don't have access to merchant payout schedules' and deflected to a dashboard/payments team, but cw-payouts states payouts run weekly on Fridays and take 2 business days (SCOPE-1: policy questions answered from the help center).

find_order/check_return_eligibility show order 2472 is $99.75 and eligible; at/below the $100 refund_auto_approve_threshold_usd it should auto-approve via issue_refund. Agent called escalate_to_human instead and told the user a human must review it, answering the user's approval question wrongly.

check_return_eligibility and get_order on order 6427 returned permission_denied (store 4, not merchant's store 1). Turn 1 confirmed the order belongs to a different store (RESP-4). Turn 2 said 'Done' and promised multi-store permissions or a refund after review, which RESP-2 and AUTH-1 do not support.

Agent escalated (correct under ESC-2) but never told the user that account changes happen only through account settings (cw-account-security), and promised 'they'll prioritize this' with no basis (RESP-5).

check_return_eligibility shows order 3255 ineligible (Juniper 14-day override, delivered 2026-06-12). Turn 1 escalated with 'may be able to work something out even though you're past the standard return window' without stating the decision; turn 2 gave the correct store-policy answer, but turn 1 had already set a false expectation (RESP-5).

Order 7230 is shipped, so it cannot be cancelled (cw-cancellations). Agent never cited cw-cancellations (RESP-1), called it 'a hard technical limit... not about a rule', gave contradictory advice ('wait for delivery, then request a return if the item hasn't been delivered yet'), and repeatedly offered escalation instead of stating the policy directly.

Agent correctly flagged order 8002's missing delivery date, but then said 'you're likely still within that window' based on the user's vague recollection, conflicting with dq-order-missing-delivery-date (do not compute a return deadline) and RESP-3.

Eligibility is correct (delivered 2026-06-01, day 30 of an inclusive 30-day window), but the agent claimed 'wrong size is a legitimate reason for a return under our policy (cw-returns)'; cw-returns lists no accepted return reasons, so it invented a rule and attributed it to a policy (RESP-1, RESP-3).

Agent made no lookup and leaked no order details (RESP-4 met), but advised the user to log into their partner's account to see order 7209, which encourages getting around the per-user access boundary (AUTH-1) and account-security norms (cw-account-security).

find_order('Harbor Knits Woven Wool Socks') returned no orders, so the agent asked for an order number or offered to list orders; acceptable. The damaged record (order 8001, dq-order-reversed-dates) was not reached.

Support may view any order (AUTH-1); get_order(8003) returned store 'Blue Heron Ceramics' and product_id 553 but not the product's store, so the store/product mismatch (dq-order-store-mismatch) was not visible in the tool result. The answer matches what the tool returned.

search_products needs a query and a store name; the request 'lowest priced items in my store' gave no query, the agent passed store '1' (the prompt has only the store id) and got not_found, then an empty result. Product 3 (dq-product-missing-title) was never returned, so the expectation was not tested. The agent did not invent a product name.
